about.title: About the data
about.what: Satellite images (Landsat 8 and 9) show how hot the ground surface is at about 10:00 local solar time. A model fills in cloudy cells and gives a 90% range. Colours on the map are surface temperature or a relative exposure index, not the air temperature.
limits: Surface temperature can be 10 to 18 °C hotter than the air in summer. It is not a heat index.
Only clear daytime satellite passes are used, so there is no night-time view and cloudy days are missing.
The grid is 30 m, but the thermal band is natively about 100 m. Do not read values as street-level accuracy.
The 90% range contained the true value about 87% of the time in testing, so treat it as slightly optimistic.
Zone boundaries are approximate and population comes from a modelled 1 km grid.
Cooling places come from OpenStreetMap volunteers and may be incomplete.
about.accuracy: On places and a year the model had never seen, the typical error was 1.4 °C, against 2.4 °C for the best simple method. This compares surface temperature with satellite data only; it was not checked against weather stations.
credits: Landsat 8 and 9 Collection 2 Level-2: USGS, via Microsoft Planetary Computer.
Elevation: Copernicus DEM GLO-30, provided by the European Union and ESA.
Boundaries and cooling places: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); locality names and shapes traced from the Nagpur Municipal Corporation intention map.
about.official: HeatSafe is a research project. It does not replace advisories from the India Meteorological Department, the National Disaster Management Authority or Nagpur Municipal Corporation.
